home.heroTitle: Is your website accessible to everyone?
home.heroSubtitle: A free website accessibility checker for NGOs and government. Enter your web address and get a clear, plain-language report of what to fix. No expertise needed. Free forever.
home.differenceBody: Most tools only run automated checks and mark the rest "needs review". We go further. Automated scanning finds the clear issues. AI-assisted review helps with the rest. And independent human review by people with lived experience of disability — launching soon — will confirm what machines cannot, producing a signed, evidence-based report, not just a list of errors.
home.step1Body: Paste the URL of the page or site you want to check.
home.step2Body: Our engine checks your pages against WCAG, the web accessibility standard.
home.step3Body: A plain-language report of what to fix first, and how to fix it.
home.sampleNote: An example report. Yours shows a score, the top issues to fix first, and how each was tested — machine, AI, or human review.
home.sampleIssue2: Text colour contrast is too low
home.persona1Body: Meet WCAG AA requirements with independent evidence — not just a self-declared statement.
home.persona2Body: Reach every person you serve — including people with disabilities.
home.persona3Body: Get verifiable accessibility evidence for due diligence.
home.persona4Body: Prioritised findings with a suggested fix, evidence, and how each was tested.
home.outcome1Body: WCAG 2.0, 2.1, 2.2 (A/AA/AAA) and Section 508, mapped to EN 301 549 and regional regulations.
home.outcome2Body: Every finding carries the affected element, page, and WCAG reference — an auditable record.
home.outcome3Body: Paid reviewers with lived experience of disability resolve what automation cannot.
home.outcome4Title: A report you can act on
home.outcome4Body: Signed, dated, and ranked by what to fix first — with a suggested fix for each issue.
home.trustPoint1: Independent human review is coming soon — we are building a review workforce with charities that serve people with visual and hearing disabilities.
home.trustPoint2: Free forever — funded by donations, not by charging for scans.
home.trustPoint3: We hold ourselves to the same standard — this site targets WCAG 2.2 AAA.
home.trustPoint4: Open about how it works — read our methodology and how we validate the engine.
home.founderBody1: Simon Mak is an entrepreneur, author, and sustainability advocate — and he lives with Parkinson's disease. He founded Ascent Partners Foundation because accessibility is not an abstract cause to him; it is personal. That is why this tool is built by people with lived experience of disability — from our founder to the review workforce we are building with disability-serving charities — for everyone who is too often excluded from the web.
home.founderBody2: His work connects finance and sustainability — and digital accessibility is the "social" in ESG.
home.founderEsgLink: See how the report maps to GRI, ESRS, and SASB

about.title: About
about.description: Ascent Partners Foundation is a Hong Kong registered charity connecting leaders with the tools to turn sustainability into action.
about.heading: About Ascent Partners Foundation
about.intro: Ascent Partners Foundation is a Hong Kong registered charity, established in 2017, that connects leaders with the ideas and tools to turn sustainability into action. We bring together decision-makers across government, civil society, and the private sector to address environmental and social challenges across the Asia-Pacific.
about.charityNote: A Hong Kong Registered Charity (IRD Section 88).
about.focus1Body: supporting climate dialogue, nature-based solutions, and decarbonisation pathways.
about.focus2Body: educational resources and guidance on environmental, social, and governance principles for businesses and practitioners.
about.focus3Body: an IUCN partnership connecting conservation initiatives with philanthropic communities, and professional conservation education.
about.toolsBody: Connecting leaders is not just about conversation — it is about giving them practical ways to act. That is why we built this accessibility assessment. An inclusive website is part of the “social” in ESG, and every leader should be able to see, in a moment, whether their site welcomes everyone. Submit a website and it checks the pages against recognised standards such as WCAG 2.2 AA, returning a plain-language score with findings and gentle guidance. It is a friendly starting point, never a verdict, and not a substitute for a certified audit.
about.peopleBody: We are a small, caring team, and we welcome people who share this mission — whether you would like help with your own site, want to contribute your expertise, or are interested in joining us. Please say hello.

humanReviewPage.title: Human review — coming soon
humanReviewPage.description: Independent human review is coming soon. We are building a review workforce in partnership with charities that serve people with visual and hearing disabilities — lived-experience experts who will verify what automation cannot.
humanReviewPage.heading: Independent human review
humanReviewPage.intro: Automated scanning and AI-assisted review resolve most success criteria today. The rest — the criteria that require judgement — will be verified by people with lived experience of disability. We are building that review workforce now, in partnership with charities that serve people with visual and hearing disabilities.
humanReviewPage.whyBody: A reviewer who navigates the web with a screen reader notices in seconds what a checklist misses — focus order that doesn't match reading order, alt text that describes the wrong thing, a form error that is announced but not actionable. That judgement turns a score into an assurance you can defend. When the service launches, reviewers will be paid for that expertise: their insight is the product, not an afterthought.
humanReviewPage.whatBody: Every success criterion the automated engine and AI cannot determine is flagged "Cannot tell". When human review launches, a reviewer whose own experience matches the barrier will resolve each one to Passed, Failed, or Not present — with a written rationale — against the exact page snapshot captured at scan time, so the result is reproducible even if the live site changes.
humanReviewPage.receiveBody: A signed, dated <link>conformance evaluation report</link>, structured like an assurance engagement: scope, evaluators, review process, per-criterion results, a conformance claim, and key findings — in-app and as a PDF, with a VPAT/ACR export for procurement.
humanReviewPage.meantimeBody: You can already run a free scan and get a partial, automated result — clearly marked as such — with a suggested fix for each issue. Independent human review will complete the picture when it launches.

forGovernment.title: For government
forGovernment.description: Independent accessibility verification for government digital and policy teams — meet WCAG AA mandates with evidence, not just a self-declared statement. Free to start.
forGovernment.heading: Accessibility assurance for government
forGovernment.intro: For digital and policy teams who must show — not just say — that public websites are accessible to everyone.
forGovernment.requirementBody: Public-sector websites are expected to meet WCAG Level AA. That is the standard behind Hong Kong's digital-government guidelines, Section 508 in the United States, EN 301 549 in Europe, and the European Accessibility Act. Citizens have a right to access public information and services — whatever their disability.
forGovernment.selfDeclaredTitle: Why a self-declared statement is not enough
forGovernment.selfDeclaredBody: Anyone can publish a conformance claim. What stands up to scrutiny is independent, evidence-based verification: a signed, dated report that shows exactly which success criteria pass, which fail, and which needed human review — with the evidence to back each one. That is what auditors, ombudsmen, and procurement teams ask for.
forGovernment.getItem1Body: automated scanning across WCAG 2.0, 2.1, 2.2 and Section 508, mapped to EN 301 549.
forGovernment.getItem2Body: the top issues to fix first, each with a suggested fix and the evidence.
forGovernment.getItem3Body: people with lived experience of disability will confirm what automation cannot.
forGovernment.getItem4Body: an auditable record for governance, procurement, and public accountability.
forGovernment.trustBody: We hold ourselves to the same standard — this site targets WCAG 2.2 AAA. Our method is open (<methodology>methodology</methodology>) and our engine is documented (<validation>how we validate it</validation>). Human review (launching soon) will be done by paid experts with lived experience of disability — not a token check.

faqPage.title: Frequently asked questions
faqPage.description: Common questions about Ascent Accessibility — costs, scanning, data, and limitations.
faqPage.heading: Frequently asked questions
faqPage.a1: Yes — single-page and whole-website scans are free for verified accounts. You just need to sign in and confirm your email.
faqPage.q2: What does a verified account unlock?
faqPage.a2: Whole-website scans (full sitemap and link crawl), the conformance table, site audit signals, PDF export, API access, and saved history — all free.
faqPage.q3: How much does AI-assisted review cost?
faqPage.a3: Bring your own key. Save your own API key for OpenRouter, OpenAI, Qwen/DashScope, Google Gemini, Anthropic, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and pay the token cost directly; the platform bears no cost and charges no fee.
faqPage.q4: How long does a scan take?
faqPage.a4: A single page usually completes in under a minute. Whole-website scans take longer — a large site can take several minutes or more. Scans run in a queue, so during busy periods they may wait.
faqPage.q5: Is a good score a guarantee of legal compliance?
faqPage.a5: No. The tool is a self-assessment aid, not a certified audit or legal advice. Automated checks cover only part of WCAG; many criteria still need manual review.
faqPage.a6: Please only scan sites you own or are authorised to assess, and use the service in line with our terms.
faqPage.a7: We store the URLs you scan, the findings, and any evidence so you can revisit your reports. You can delete assessments from your history at any time. See the privacy policy for detail.
faqPage.a8: From the billing portal on the site scans page — cancellation takes effect at the end of the current billing period.

primer.title: What is web accessibility?
primer.description: A plain-language introduction to web accessibility for NGOs and government — what it means, who it affects, why it matters, and how to start. No jargon.
primer.heading: What is web accessibility?
primer.intro: A plain-language introduction — no jargon, no prior knowledge needed.
primer.shortBody1: Web accessibility means that everyone can use your website — including people with disabilities. A person who is blind, has low vision, cannot hear, has limited movement, or finds some content hard to understand should still be able to read, navigate, and use what you publish.
primer.shortBody2: It is not a special feature for a few people. It is simply a website that works for everyone.
primer.whoBody1: Around one in six people live with a disability. Barriers can be visual, hearing, motor, or cognitive — and they can be permanent (blindness), temporary (a broken arm), or situational (bright sunlight on a phone screen, or holding a baby).
primer.whoBody2: Designing for people with disabilities usually makes things better for everyone.
primer.whyItem1Body: You serve your whole community, not just part of it.
primer.whyItem2Body: Everyone deserves equal access to public information and services.
primer.whyItem3Body: Many governments and funders ask for it by law or policy.
primer.pourIntro: WCAG — the web accessibility standard — groups everything into four principles:
primer.pour1Body: People can see or hear the content (for example, images have text alternatives).
primer.pour2Body: People can use it (for example, everything works with a keyboard).
primer.pour3Body: People can follow it (clear language, predictable behaviour).
primer.pour4Body: It works with the tools people use, now and in the future.
primer.toolsBody: People browse the web in many ways: a screen reader (reads the page aloud), screen magnification, keyboard-only navigation, voice control, or a switch device. A good website works with all of them.
primer.standardBody: WCAG (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines) is the international standard. It has three levels — A, AA, and AAA. Most laws and policies ask for level AA. This site itself targets AAA, the highest level. <link1>Browse the WCAG criteria</link1> or look up any term in our <link2>plain-language glossary</link2>.
primer.startBody: You do not need to be an expert. Run a free scan of your site to see where you stand, or take the free course to learn at your own pace.

methodology.title: Methodology
methodology.description: How Ascent Accessibility scores a website — crawling, the Ascent Accessibility engine, site audit signals, and the scoring model.
methodology.heading: Methodology
methodology.intro: A transparent account of how the assessment works, so you know what a score means — and what it cannot tell you.
methodology.crawlBody: Whole-website scans start with the site's sitemap.xml, falling back to a link crawl, and respect robots.txt. Crawling is bounded by a depth and a page cap, so very large sites may be reported as covering a subset of pages.
methodology.scanBody: Each page is scanned with the Ascent Accessibility engine — an in-house, clean-room WCAG rule engine — against the rules for the standard you selected. Automated rules detect only issues that can be identified automatically, roughly 30–50% of WCAG criteria. A companion site audit measures performance, SEO, and best-practice signals, and an optional AI-assisted review narrows the items that require manual judgement.
methodology.scoreBody: The score starts at 100 and subtracts a fixed weight per finding — critical −10, serious −5, moderate −2, minor −0.5 — capped per finding. 90+ is a pass, 70–89 is partial, and below 70 is a fail. The conformance table separately tracks which success criteria pass, fail, are not applicable, or need manual review.
methodology.limitsBody: Automated tools cannot judge meaning, so many criteria (for example, whether alt text is accurate, or whether content is genuinely understandable) require human review. A clean score is encouraging, but it is not a certificate of conformance. Treat the report as a starting point for a manual review.
methodology.seeAll: See the full list of <link>WCAG 2.2 success criteria</link> the tool scores against.
